Every peptide in every biological sample, as log2 intensity or NA with the reason, by mzLib

diff_observations.Rd

Build mzLib's observation table from a stored FlashLFQ or MetaMorpheus peptide table: every peptide in every biological sample as log2 intensity or no value with the reason, with the shared-peptide normalization shifts, and optionally the peptide-by-sample table stats fit reads.

mzLib's FlashLfqObservations.FromPeptideTable reads a stored FlashLFQ or MetaMorpheus peptide table, maps each run's detection type to a state, sums each technical replicate's fractions on the linear scale and averages a sample's replicates in log2. Then SharedPeptideNormalization.Measure measures how far each sample sits from the others on the peptides they share; normalize = TRUE subtracts it.

Usage

diff_observations(peptides, runs, basis, protein_groups = NULL, samples = NULL,
  normalize = FALSE, min_peptides = NULL, out = NULL, responses_out = NULL,
  timeout = 600)

Arguments

peptides

A FlashLFQ QuantifiedPeptides.tsv or a MetaMorpheus AllQuantifiedPeptides.tsv.

runs

Every run of the table, as a data.frame with file and sample columns, and optionally fraction and technical_replicate (whole numbers; NA or absent sends none, so mzLib's 0). file is the run's name as the Intensity_ columns write it, without extension; a column with -calib after it matches too. The result's own runs is accepted as well.

basis

"msms_only" (no match-between-runs value enters) or "mbr_kept". Required: mzLib has no default.

protein_groups

A MetaMorpheus AllQuantifiedProteinGroups.tsv, for each group's q-value and decoy, contaminant and entrapment flags. NULL: none described.

samples

A TSV whose first column (after a header row) lists the samples to keep, e.g. one stratum's design file from diff_design. NULL: every sample.

normalize

Subtract each sample's shift. The shifts are measured and reported either way.

min_peptides

The floor on the normalization's reference set (peptides). NULL: not sent, so mzLib's own floor, 100 at mzLib d10017ce.

out

A .tsv path to write the long table to instead of returning its rows.

responses_out

A .tsv path to also write the peptide-by-sample log2 table that stats_fit reads as responses.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Value

An mzlibr_observations:

- records, a data.frame with one row per (peptide, sample), peptides ordinal by full sequence: full_sequence, the engine's modified sequence, the key; base_sequence; protein_groups, a list column of every group the peptide table names (UNDEFINED = in no surviving group); unique_protein_group, the one group it is unique to, NA when shared, UNDEFINED or none; sample; log2_intensity (log2 of FlashLFQ intensity units), fractions summed, replicates averaged in log2, less the shift with normalize = TRUE, and NA for no value (see state), never 0; and state, one of "quantified", "mbr_transferred", "ambiguous_peak", "identified_not_quantified" or "not_detected". Empty with out. - peptides_file, protein_groups_file and samples_file as absolute paths, the last two NA when not given; basis and normalize as given; min_peptides (peptides) as given, NA when mzLib's floor applied; run_count runs; runs, a data.frame of the runs as mzLib holds them (file_name, sample_id, fraction, technical_replicate), ordinal by file name; sample_count samples; samples; samples_without_values; peptide_count peptides; protein_group_count protein groups; protein_groups, a data.frame of those groups (name, q_value a fraction 0 to 1 or NA if not finite, is_decoy, is_contaminant, is_entrapment, genes or NA); state_counts, rows (cells) per state; warnings; written (path, format, row_count) or NULL; responses_written (path, format, row_count peptides, sample_count samples) or NULL; row_count rows, peptide_count x sample_count; column_names. - normalization, mzLib's NormalizationResult, measured whether or not it was applied: setting, "shared_peptide_median" (the peptides with a value in every sample), "shared_peptide_median_half" (in at least half; used when too few are in all) or "none" (too few either way: no sample shifted); reference_set_size (peptides) in the set used; minimum_reference_set_size (peptides), the floor used; shifts, each sample's shift in log2 units, NA for a sample with no shift; and warnings. - caveats: how values are combined, what the basis does, what mzLib cannot check about the table, and what the normalization assumes.

The traps

Median normalization assumes most peptides do not change between samples. When most of them do - a table of the spiked organism alone, a loading series, a pull-down - normalizing deletes the result: read normalization$shifts before you subtract them. The peptide table does not record the design FlashLFQ quantified with, so give the runs that design. mzLib does not yet roll peptides up to proteins or choose a test's rows, so neither does this.

Wraps

Wire verb diff observations. Generated from the bridge's verb spec diff.observations.yaml (bridge commit 60b1d25968a1) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • FlashLfqObservations.ReadProteinGroups in mzLib/FlashLFQ/Differential/FlashLfqObservations.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • ObservationTable in mzLib/Quantification/Differential/ObservationTable.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • ObservationTable.ForSamples in mzLib/Quantification/Differential/ObservationTable.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • ObservationRun in mzLib/Quantification/Differential/ObservationTable.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • QuantBasis in mzLib/Quantification/Differential/ObservationTable.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SharedPeptideNormalization.DefaultMinimumPeptides in mzLib/Quantification/Differential/SharedPeptideNormalization.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

peptides

path; required. A FlashLFQ QuantifiedPeptides.tsv, or a MetaMorpheus AllQuantifiedPeptides.tsv (mzLib picks the reader by that name ending). Its Intensity_ and Detection Type_ columns are the runs. An IsoTracker table is refused.

basis

string; required; range msms_only | mbr_kept. Which match-between-runs values enter (mzLib's QuantBasis, by its machine name). msms_only: no transferred value enters a sum. mbr_kept: the transferred values FlashLFQ kept enter. Required: mzLib has no default, because it is a scientific choice.

runs (wire --stdin)

string[]; required; range >= 1 line; file, sample, then optionally fraction and technical replicate, tab-separated. The experimental design's runs, one per line: the file as the table's Intensity_ columns name it, without its extension (a column with -calib after that name matches too); the biological sample it belongs to; then optionally its fraction and its technical replicate (integers; left out, ObservationRun's default 0). Every run the table has must be given, and only those. Grouping comes only from these lines: a file name is never parsed for it.

protein_groups (wire --protein-groups)

path; default absent. A MetaMorpheus AllQuantifiedProteinGroups.tsv, read by FlashLfqObservations.ReadProteinGroups for each group's q-value and its decoy, contaminant and entrapment flags. Absent, no group is described: mzLib then warns, and no peptide can be kept out of the normalization reference as a decoy or contaminant.

samples

path; default absent. A TSV with a header row whose first column lists the samples to keep (ObservationTable.ForSamples), such as a sample sheet or a design file from diff design. Narrow to one stratum this way: the normalization is measured over every sample of the table it is given. Absent, every sample is kept.

normalize

flag; default FALSE. Subtract each sample's shift from its log2 values (SharedPeptideNormalization.Apply). The shifts are measured and reported either way.

min_peptides (wire --min-peptides)

int; in peptides; default absent; range >= 1. The floor on either normalization reference set (Measure's minimumPeptides). Absent, the bridge sends none and mzLib's SharedPeptideNormalization.DefaultMinimumPeptides applies: 100 at this pin. Below the floor on the every-sample set mzLib tries the half-samples set, and below it there too no sample is shifted (setting none).

out

path; default absent; range a .tsv path. Write the long table here (header, then one line per row; protein_groups ';'-joined; an empty cell for null) instead of returning its rows. Absent, the rows are returned.

responses_out (wire --responses-out)

path; default absent; range a .tsv path. Also write the table's own peptide-by-sample shape: header full_sequence then the samples, one row per peptide, each cell ObservationTable.Log2Intensity in round-trip decimal (after --normalize, if given) or empty for no value. Exactly what stats fit --responses reads. Peptides only: mzLib does not yet roll peptides up to proteins or choose a test's rows.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

peptides_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the peptide table.

protein_groups_file

string; NA when no --protein-groups. Absolute path of the protein-group table.

samples_file

string; NA when no --samples: every sample was kept. Absolute path of the sample list.

basis

string; never NA. msms_only or mbr_kept, as given.

normalize

bool; never NA. Whether the shifts were subtracted (--normalize).

min_peptides

int; in peptides; NA when not given: mzLib's DefaultMinimumPeptides applied (normalization.minimum_reference_set_size says which). --min-peptides as given.

run_count

int; in runs; never NA. Runs in the table (after --samples).

runs

object[]; never NA. ObservationTable.Runs, ordinal by file name: file_name, sample_id, fraction and technical_replicate, as mzLib holds them.

sample_count

int; in samples; never NA. Biological samples: the distinct samples of the runs (after --samples).

samples

string[]; never NA. The samples, ordinal by id: every sample, with or without values.

samples_without_values

string[]; never NA. Samples in which no peptide has a value under this basis (a lost run).

peptide_count

int; in peptides; never NA. Peptides (distinct full sequences); the table has peptide_count x sample_count rows.

protein_group_count

int; in protein groups; never NA. Groups described by --protein-groups; 0 without it.

protein_groups

object[]; never NA. Each described group: name (MetaMorpheus's, member accessions joined by |), q_value (fraction 0 to 1; null if not finite), is_decoy, is_contaminant, is_entrapment, genes (null when the table has none).

state_counts

map<string,int>; in cells; never NA. Rows per state, keyed by every state in mzLib's order: quantified, mbr_transferred, ambiguous_peak, identified_not_quantified, not_detected.

normalization

object; never NA. mzLib's NormalizationResult, measured whether or not --normalize applied it; fields under result.tables.normalization.

warnings

string[]; never NA. ObservationTable.Warnings: what the reader should know that did not stop the build, e.g. protein groups the peptides name that the protein-group table does not describe.

written

object; NA when no --out: the rows are in columns. path (absolute), format (tsv) and row_count of the long table written.

responses_written

object; NA when no --responses-out. path (absolute), format (tsv), row_count (peptides) and sample_count of the responses table written.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. peptide_count x sample_count, returned or written.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per (peptide, sample): peptides ordinal by full sequence, each peptide's samples in order. Empty with --out.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Six static caveats, plus one without --protein-groups and one when the normalization setting is none.

Columns of records

full_sequence

string; never NA. The engine's full (modified) sequence: the peptide's key, unique in the table.

base_sequence

string; never NA. The unmodified sequence.

protein_groups

string[]; never NA. Every group the peptide table's Protein Groups cell names, distinct and ordinal-sorted; UNDEFINED is MetaMorpheus's placeholder for a peptide in no surviving group; empty when the cell is blank.

unique_protein_group

string; NA when shared (two or more groups), only UNDEFINED, or no group. The one group the peptide is unique to (ObservedPeptide.UniqueProteinGroup). Sharing counts against every group written, whatever its q-value.

sample

string; never NA. The biological sample.

log2_intensity

float; in log2 of FlashLFQ intensity units; NA when no value: state says why. log2 of the sample's intensity: each technical replicate's fractions summed on the linear scale, then the replicates' log2 values averaged; minus the sample's shift with --normalize. Never 0 for missing.

state

string; never NA. Where the value came from, or why there is none (mzLib's ObservationState; a sample without a value takes the most informative state among its runs): quantified (MS/MS-identified peaks only) | mbr_transferred (a match-between-runs peak is in the value; under msms_only the value is left out and log2_intensity is null) | ambiguous_peak (a peak withheld as ambiguous; no value) | identified_not_quantified (identified by MS/MS, no peak; no value) | not_detected (no value).

Fields of normalization

normalization$setting (wire setting)

string; never NA. Which reference set the shifts were measured on: shared_peptide_median (peptides with a value in every sample with values) | shared_peptide_median_half (in at least half of them and at least 2; used when the every-sample set is under the floor) | none (both under the floor: no sample shifted).

normalization$reference_set_size (wire reference_set_size)

int; in peptides; never NA. Peptides in the reference set used, or in the last set tried when setting is none. Peptides of decoy, contaminant or entrapment groups never enter it.

normalization$minimum_reference_set_size (wire minimum_reference_set_size)

int; in peptides; never NA. The floor used: --min-peptides, else mzLib's DefaultMinimumPeptides.

normalization$shifts (wire shifts)

map<string,float>; in log2 units; never NA. Each sample's shift, subtracted from its values with --normalize: the median, over the reference peptides it has, of its value minus the peptide's mean over the samples that have it. On the half set mzLib repeats that until the shifts settle and centres them to average 0 within each group of linked samples. A value is null when undefined (no reference peptide has a value in that sample, or setting none); that sample is not shifted.

normalization$warnings (wire warnings)

string[]; never NA. Which samples have no shift and why, and whether the half set did not settle or fell into unlinked groups.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--peptides or --basis missing; --basis not msms_only or mbr_kept; --protein-groups, --samples, --out or --responses-out given without a value; a file not found, or not the table type named; --out or --responses-out not ending in .tsv; --min-peptides below 1 or not an integer

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

no runs on stdin; a run line with other than 2 to 4 fields, an empty file or sample, or a fraction or technical replicate that is not an integer; the --samples file empty, header-only or with an empty first cell

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the input (its ArgumentException, reclassified): two runs with one file name or one place (sample, replicate, fraction); a table column no run matches, or a run no column matches; IsoTracker output; a blank, negative or non-finite intensity or an unreadable detection type; a peptide listed twice; a group name holding ';'; a --samples id the table does not have

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • A missing value is null, never 0, and state says why. Fractions of one technical replicate are summed on the linear scale, then a sample's technical replicates are averaged on the log2 scale (mzLib's ObservationTable).

  • Under msms_only a match-between-runs value enters no sum, but its cell still says mbr_transferred; under mbr_kept it enters, and the cell says mbr_transferred.

  • The peptide table does not record the design FlashLFQ quantified with, so mzLib cannot check that these runs group the files as FlashLFQ did. FlashLFQ withholds every fraction of a sample whose strongest fraction is ambiguous; give the runs the design it quantified with, or a value it withheld can become a partial sum.

  • FlashLFQ writes its peptide table in the culture of the machine it ran on and mzLib reads it as invariant (a decimal point), so a table written where the decimal separator is a comma does not read correctly.

  • Every peptide is a row: decoy, contaminant and entrapment peptides, and peptides of groups at any q-value, included. mzLib does not yet choose the rows a differential test uses, or roll peptides up to proteins, so --responses-out is peptide by sample only. Filter rows with protein_groups and unique_protein_group.

  • The normalization shifts are always measured (SharedPeptideNormalization.Measure) over every sample of the table, after --samples; they are subtracted only with --normalize. Measure one stratum at a time. A sample whose shift is null is not shifted.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::diff::observations_with with ObservationsOptions

References

  • doi:10.1021/acs.jproteome.7b00608: FlashLFQ, whose peptide table and detection types this verb reads (Millikin et al., J Proteome Res 2018)

  • doi:10.1186/gb-2010-11-10-r106: the median-of-ratios idea the shared-peptide normalization follows: each sample against the log of a geometric-mean reference (Anders and Huber, Genome Biol 11:R106, 2010)

See also

diff_design, stats_fit, flashlfq_quantify

Examples


# Two runs of FlashLFQ's E. coli spike-in vignette, which their names say were spiked at 1x and
# at 2x:
peptides <- system.file("extdata", "diff", "EcoliSpikeIn_QuantifiedPeptides.tsv",
  package = "mzLibR")
runs <- data.frame(
  file = c("09-04-18_EcoliSpikeInSingleShot1x", "09-04-18_EcoliSpikeInSingleShot2x"),
  sample = c("spike_1x", "spike_2x"))
table <- diff_observations(peptides, runs, basis = "msms_only")
table
#> <mzlibr_observations> 243 peptides x 2 samples, msms_only
#>   quantified 319, mbr_transferred 43, ambiguous_peak 9, identified_not_quantified 6, not_detected 109
#>   normalization: none on 86 peptides
table$state_counts
#>                quantified           mbr_transferred            ambiguous_peak 
#>                       319                        43                         9 
#> identified_not_quantified              not_detected 
#>                         6                       109 
table$normalization[c("setting", "reference_set_size")]
#> $setting
#> [1] "none"
#> 
#> $reference_set_size
#> [1] 86
#>
